# Non-Parametric Tests {#sec-np}

Non-parametric tests do not assume a specific distribution. They work on
**ranks** instead of raw values, which makes them robust to outliers and
skew --- useful for latency, memory, and other CS quantities
[@arcuri2014hitchhiker].

## Mann–Whitney U (Wilcoxon Rank-Sum)

The non-parametric counterpart to the independent-samples t-test.

```r
wilcox.test(A, B, conf.int = TRUE)
```

It tests whether one distribution tends to produce larger values than the
other (stochastic dominance), not equality of medians per se.

## Wilcoxon Signed-Rank

Paired counterpart of the paired t-test.

```r
wilcox.test(optimized, baseline, paired = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```

## Kruskal–Wallis

Non-parametric one-way ANOVA.

```r
kruskal.test(latency ~ scheduler, data = data)
```

If significant, follow up with pairwise Wilcoxon with adjustment:

```r
pairwise.wilcox.test(data$latency, data$scheduler,
                     p.adjust.method = "holm")
```

## Permutation Tests

Conceptually the cleanest non-parametric idea: under $H_0$, group labels are
exchangeable. Shuffle them many times and see how often a statistic at least
as extreme as the observed one arises.

```r
perm_test <- function(x, y, R = 10000) {
  obs <- mean(x) - mean(y)
  combined <- c(x, y)
  n1 <- length(x)
  stats <- replicate(R, {
    idx <- sample(length(combined))
    mean(combined[idx[1:n1]]) -
      mean(combined[idx[(n1+1):length(combined)]])
  })
  mean(abs(stats) >= abs(obs))
}
perm_test(A, B)
```

## Effect Sizes for Non-Parametric Tests

```r
library(effsize)
cliff.delta(A, B)
```

`cliff.delta` is the recommended effect size in non-parametric CS
comparisons.
